sections.h2: Where does a Wayne County seller record a deed?
sections.html:
Deeds for Wayne County land are recorded at the Wayne County Register of Deeds, 400 Monroe, 7th floor, in the Greektown district of downtown Detroit. The county describes the 7th floor as sitting above a restaurant on Monroe, and the Treasurer's deed certification desk is on the 5th floor of the same building.

Since October 1, 2025 the office has worked by appointment only. A person cannot wait on the floor for a slot to open. The first appointments of the day start at 8:00 AM and the last start at 3:50 PM. A 20 minute appointment covers up to five documents, and a 45 minute appointment is meant for high volume customers who record five to 25. Only one person per appointment may enter. Call 313-224-5860 for help with scheduling, or 313-224-5851 with recording questions.

Documents can also be mailed in. Hand delivered documents must be picked up by the same firm or agent that dropped them off, while mailed ones go back to the return address printed on the document. That address is often the attorney or title agent, not the buyer.

sections.h2: What does Wayne County charge to record a document?
sections.html:
The office raised its fee schedule effective January 1, 2026, and says it was the first increase since 1996. A deed, mortgage or other instrument not listed separately costs $26.00 plus a $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee, for $30.00 per document regardless of page count.

Wayne County recording, search and certification charges as printed on the county's Register of Deeds and Treasurer pages

The county adds that its recording fees may differ from those of other counties, so a figure quoted for a neighboring county does not carry over.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax calculated and paid in Wayne County?
sections.html:
The county prints the formula itself: county tax of $0.55 per $500 and state tax of $3.75 per $500, which it restates as $8.60 per $1,000 of the consideration amount. It is paid when the deed is recorded, unless a proper exemption is written on the document.

Transfer tax must be paid in cash, check or money order payable to the Wayne County Register of Deeds. The statute lists the exemptions, and the ones a house seller meets most often are these, from MCL 207.526:

  • a sale where the consideration is under $100
  • a conveyance from an individual to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild
  • a transfer given in foreclosure, or in lieu of foreclosure, of a mortgage
  • a land contract in which legal title has not yet passed to the buyer
  • a court order that does not state a specific price

The county's list of common rejections says a deed must either cite the consideration or cite the exemption statute and subparagraph, with MCL 207.505 for the county tax and MCL 207.526 for the state tax. Sellers who held a principal residence exemption can also read subsection (u) of the state act, which allows a refund request in some cases where the assessed value has not risen since the home was first assessed.

sections.h2: Which forms of payment does the Wayne County office accept?
sections.html:
The counter takes credit and debit cards when the cardholder has a matching ID, plus money orders, cashier's checks, certified checks, corporation checks and law firm checks. American Express and Discover are not accepted. Personal checks are refused at the counter but are accepted for mail transactions, while cards are not accepted by mail.

Every document should come with its own check covering fees and transfer tax. The rules on the amount are strict:

  • If the check is short, the document and check come back unprocessed.
  • If the check is more than $25.00 over, everything is returned.
  • If the overage is $25.00 or less, the document is recorded and the extra is not refunded.
  • If a group of documents arrives on one check and any one fails the requirements, the whole group is returned.

A seller who uses a title company rarely handles any of this. A seller who records alone, for example a family transfer, should price the check exactly.

sections.h2: What makes a Wayne County deed recordable?
sections.html:
The county publishes a checklist, and its rejection list shows where deeds fail. Signatures must be original, with names typed, printed or stamped beneath them. A deed signed in Michigan that conveys real estate needs a notary acknowledgment, and the drafter's name and address must appear on it.

  • Paper is white, 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches, with black ink and at least 10 point type.
  • The first page needs a 2.5 inch top margin, and every other margin is at least 0.5 inch.
  • The title of the document goes on the first line of print, and the parcel number and commonly known address should appear.
  • A complete legal description is needed: city, lot numbers, subdivision name, plat liber and page, or condominium unit and master deed details.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number must be obscured or removed.
  • A death certificate must be an original certified by the clerk, and a court order must be certified and sealed.

The office does not provide blank documents and is barred from giving legal advice. It recommends working with an attorney to prepare them.

sections.h2: Why does the Wayne County Treasurer certify deeds before they are recorded?
sections.html:
Michigan law makes the register of deeds ask for proof that taxes on the property are paid for the five years before the date of the instrument. MCL 211.135 lists the certificates, and without them the instrument is not recorded. Wayne County requires this tax certification on warranty deeds, deeds with a covenant of warranty, land contracts and assignments of land contracts.

The Treasurer certifies the original document only, because copies cannot be certified. You can book a separate appointment at the Treasurer's office and then take the document to the Register, or mail the original by UPS, FedEx or USPS with a check to the Wayne County Treasurer and a stamped return envelope. The Treasurer then mails it back and you forward it for recording. If a document has more than 25 parcel numbers, the fee is $5.00 plus 20 cents for each parcel over 25.

Delinquent tax is the usual obstacle. Under the Treasurer's explanation, tax unpaid to the local treasurer by the last day of February turns delinquent on March 1, and from then it can be paid only to the county. A parcel delinquent for a full year reaches forfeited status the next March 1, and the interest rate moves from 1% to 1.5% per month, with a $175 foreclosure fee and $30 in recording fees added.

sections.h2: How big is the Wayne County recording workload?
sections.html:
Wayne County is the most populous county in Michigan. It was founded in 1796, and the Register describes the office as the library of land records for nearly 900,000 parcels, with records filed under liber and page numbers back to 1703. Detroit is the county seat and largest city, and the southern communities are known as Downriver.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 1,769,038 residents on 611.84 square miles of land, with 814,793 housing units. About 64.8% of homes are owner occupied, the median value of an owner occupied home is $178,500, and the median household income is $60,539 (2020 to 2024 figures). Building permits numbered 3,922 in 2025.

With that many parcels, appointment slots are a real constraint. Book early when a closing date depends on a recorded deed, and let the title company confirm which of its documents need tax certification first.

sections.h2: How do you find or copy a recorded Wayne County deed?
sections.html:
There are three routes: the county land records website, a visit to the office, or a search by mail. The website runs around the clock. A free public search lists documents by grantor or grantee name only and does not show the document. The pay as you go On-Demand Account opens searches by address, legal description, parcel number or liber and page, and prints at $2 per page. Certified copies are not available online.

At the office, kiosks in the lobby let you search yourself. Veterans and current military personnel may receive a search of their own property and copies of its documents free of charge when they present credentials, though commercial enterprises are excluded. A mailed request needs a short description, a check to the Wayne County Register of Deeds, and the address 400 Monroe, 7th Floor, Detroit, MI 48226. The county's pages give two different starting years for online images, so ask the office what date range your search needs before paying for a session.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Wayne County?
faqs.a: The charge is $30.00 per document, made up of $26.00 plus the $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee. The schedule took effect January 1, 2026. A warranty deed also needs the Treasurer's tax certification at $5.00 per document.

faqs.q: Do I need an appointment to record a deed at the Wayne County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. Appointments have been required since October 1, 2025, and walk-ins cannot wait for an opening. Book the service you need (record, search or kiosk) on the county's calendar, or call 313-224-5860.

faqs.q: What is the Wayne County transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The county prints $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, also stated as $8.60 per $1,000 of consideration. It is due at recording unless an exemption is cited on the deed.

faqs.q: Can the Register of Deeds prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not provide or prepare blank documents and may not give legal advice. It recommends that an attorney prepare your deed so it meets the recording rules.

faqs.q: Why would Wayne County reject my deed?
faqs.a: Common reasons are a copied signature, a missing consideration amount or exemption citation, wrong margins or font size, an incomplete legal description, and a missing treasurer certification. Rejected documents go back with the check for correction.
